Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll. As full-time employee, max is write unless their role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll, so admin is not allowed. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E022 (Timothy Wallace) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Timothy Wallace (E022) requests admin access to Payroll. Admin is not allowed: Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and the employee's role is Engineer (so the full-time admin exception does not apply), and contractors can never have admin. The notes conflict on employment type (full-time vs. contractor with basic security training). Applying the most restrictive valid policy — contractor with basic training — the maximum is read, and the requested admin exceeds it. Grant the maximum: read.
